Before Xi Jinping's visit to the US, Taiwanese worry about postponed arms deliveries
subhead: Donald Trump described US arms sales to Taiwan as a 'negotiating chip' with China following his trip in May. But by tying these deliveries to broader negotiations, Washington is undermining its longstanding support for Taiwan.

title: One year after the Gen Z movement, Morocco's youth remain largely absent from parliamentary elections
subhead: Few Moroccans under 30 – a demographic that has felt ignored by political parties and institutions – are running as candidates. Young Moroccans will likely demonstrate their disillusionment through massive abstention in the September 23 elections.

title: UN chief says fossil fuel majors treat atmosphere like 'open sewer'
subhead: Antonio Guterres slammed the energy industry at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday. 'Those who polluted the most, and profited the most, must do far more to repair the damage they caused,' he urged.

title: The Catholic Church's new power players: Americans
subhead: They hold key positions at the Holy See and are establishing think tanks, foundations and universities in Rome. In the wake of their compatriot Robert Prevost, who became Pope Leo XIV in 2025 and whose popularity continues to grow in the United States, American Catholics are throwing their full weight into shaping Catholicism.

title: 'Maoism took root in very diverse places and moments due to its multi-faceted, contradictory and malleable nature'
subhead: 'Mao's Fraught Legacy' (7/7). Julia Lovell, a Chinese history and literature professor at Birkbeck, University of London, discusses how Maoism spread. The ideology, she says, benefited from the broader decolonization era, with Mao seen as the foremost anti-imperialist figure.

title: At Dati's Renault corruption trial, a damning testimony and awkward memos
subhead: Taking the stand on Monday, MEP Daniel Freund said former French minister Rachida Dati had told the European Parliament she worked as a lawyer on 'domestic violence' cases.
